arxiv-2106-12051.title: More stochastic expansions for the pricing of vanilla options with cash dividends
arxiv-2106-12051.creator: Fabien Le Floc’h
arxiv-2106-12051.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Fabien Le Floc’h. There is no exact closed form formula for pricing of European options with discrete cash dividends under the model where the underlying asset price follows a piecewise lognormal process with jumps at dividend ex-dates. This paper presents alternative expansions based on the technique of Etore and Gobet, leading to more robust first, second and third-order expansions across the range of strikes and the range of dividend dates.

arxiv-2207-01466.title: Physics-informed compressed sensing for PC-MRI: an inverse Navier–Stokes problem
arxiv-2207-01466.creator: Alexandros Kontogiannis, Matthew P. Juniper
arxiv-2207-01466.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alexandros Kontogiannis, Matthew P. Juniper. We formulate a physics-informed compressed sensing (PICS) method for the reconstruction of velocity fields from noisy and sparse phase-contrast magnetic resonance signals. The method solves an inverse Navier–Stokes boundary value problem, which permits us to jointly reconstruct and segment the velocity field, and at the same time infer hidden quantities such as the hydrodynamic pressure and the wall shear stress.

arxiv-2403-09503.title: Shrinkage for Extreme Partial Least-Squares
arxiv-2403-09503.creator: Julyan Arbel, Stéphane Girard & Hadrien Lorenzo
arxiv-2403-09503.description: Abstract Abstract This work focuses on dimension-reduction techniques for modelling conditional extreme values. Specifically, we investigate the idea that extreme values of a response variable can be explained by nonlinear functions derived from linear projections of an input random vector.

arxiv-2407-15054.title: Enhancing K-user Interference Alignment for Discrete Constellations via Learning
arxiv-2407-15054.creator: Rajesh Mishra, Syed Jafar, Sriram Vishwanath, Hyeji Kim
arxiv-2407-15054.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rajesh Mishra, Syed Jafar, Sriram Vishwanath, Hyeji Kim. In this paper, we consider a K K -user interference channel where interference among the users is neither too strong nor too weak , a scenario that is relatively underexplored in the literature. We propose a novel deep learning-based approach to design the encoder and decoder functions that aim to maximize the sumrate of the interference channel for discrete constellations.

arxiv-2503-01403.title: Inverse nodal problems for Dirac differential operators with jump condition.
arxiv-2503-01403.creator: Baki Keskin
arxiv-2503-01403.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Baki Keskin. This paper deals with an inverse nodal problem for the Dirac differential operator with the discontinuity conditions inside the interval. We obtain a new approach for asymptotic expressions of the solutions and prove that the coefficients of the Dirac system can be determined uniquely by a dense subset of the nodal points (zeros of the first component of the eigenfunction). We also provide an algorithm for constructing the solution of this inverse nodal problem.

arxiv-2509-08617.title: Towards Interpretable Deep Neural Networks for Tabular Data
arxiv-2509-08617.creator: Khawla Elhadri, Jörg Schlötterer, Christin Seifert
arxiv-2509-08617.description: Abstract Tabular data is the foundation of many applications in fields such as finance and healthcare. Although DNNs tailored for tabular data achieve competitive predictive performance, they are blackboxes with little interpretability. We introduce XNNTab , a neural architecture that uses a sparse autoencoder (SAE) to learn a dictionary of monosemantic features within the latent space used for prediction.

arxiv-2512-24682.title: CellSecInspector : Safeguarding Cellular Networks via Automated Security Analysis on Specifications Conference: Preprint; Preprint; Preprint
arxiv-2512-24682.creator: Ke Xie, Xingyi Zhao, Yiwen Hu, Munshi Saifuzzaman, Wen Li, Shuhan Yuan, Tian Xie, Guan-Hua Tu
arxiv-2512-24682.description: Abstract . The complexity, interdependence, and rapid evolution of 3GPP specifications present fundamental challenges for ensuring the security of modern cellular networks. Manual reviews and existing automated approaches, which often depend on rule-based parsing or small sets of manually crafted security requirements, fail to capture deep semantic dependencies, cross-sentence/clause relationships, and evolving specification behaviors.

pmc-11508790.description: Cotton (Gossypium spp.) is the most important fibre crop worldwide.
